#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""VelaPaw patch #36 -- revert #35's guards, expose an RX kick.

Applies ON TOP of #33 + #34 + #35 (driver must be 115,107 bytes).

TWO CHANGES.

1. REVERT patch #35 half 1 (the four same-value reconfigure guards).

   Half 1 did exactly what it was built to do -- b78 measured `cfgskip 20
   chst 1 resc 0`, i.e. every redundant reconfigure declined and zero channel
   restarts -- and the capture stalled anyway, in both of its flavours
   (`eof 0 start 1` and `eof 1 start 2`).  So the redundant reconfigures were
   not the cause and the guards buy nothing.

   Worse, they cost something.  i2s_rx_channel_start() is the only code in
   this driver that resets the RX module, the RX FIFO and the GDMA IN channel,
   and the redundant reconfigure was the only thing that ever reached it after
   boot.  With #35 half 1 in place, `chst` never leaves 1 -- so the one lever
   that could un-wedge a stalled RX channel is gone.  Reverting restores it.

   The `intraw 000000a0` reading that motivated #35 is also withdrawn: it is
   now known to be bit-identical across four stalled dumps and three builds,
   including one where the ISR never ran to clear it, so it is stale
   boot-time state and not evidence of a mid-flight FIFO event.

2. KEEP #35 half 2 (the rescue in i2s_rx_channel_start), and expose the same
   recovery to the app as velapaw_i2s_rx_kick().

   WHY THE APP NEEDS ITS OWN LEVER.  When a capture times out, mic.c's failure
   path calls mic_session_close(), and that is where the voice worker HANGS --
   `caps 1 / lastret -999 / stage 32 (session-close)` says velapaw_mic_capture()
   never returned at all.  One capture per boot is attempted, ever.  So any
   recovery built out of AUDIOIOC_STOP / CONFIGURE / START is built out of the
   very calls that are suspected of blocking, and a retry loop made of them
   would hang on its first iteration.

   velapaw_i2s_rx_kick() sidesteps all of it.  It touches only registers and
   this driver's own queues, takes priv->slock, and cannot block: no ioctl, no
   codec worker thread, no message queue.  The app can call it directly (flat
   build, same address space) the same way it already externs the #33/#34
   probes.

   It does what i2s_rx_channel_start() does to the hardware -- stop RX, stop
   the inlink, reset the GDMA IN channel, reset the RX module and RX FIFO,
   pulse RX_UPDATE -- then clears the latched GDMA interrupt bits, rescues any
   container the reset just orphaned back onto rx.pend, and re-arms.

   Clearing DMA_IN_INT_CLR matters for its own sake: nothing has written it
   since boot in a stalled run, which is exactly why intraw has been reading
   the same stale 0xa0 every time.  After a kick, intraw means something again.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM.  The kick does not fix the underlying fault, which is
still unidentified and still looks to sit below the DMA.  It makes the stall
recoverable instead of terminal, and it makes the retry testable -- we have
never once observed what a second capture attempt does, because there has never
been a second attempt.

Writes <file>.new and os.replace()s it.  --dry checks anchors only.
"""

import hashlib
import io
import os
import sys

SRC = os.path.expanduser(
    "~/openvela/nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_i2s.c")

# Clean b68 + #33 + #34 + #35, i.e. exactly the b78 driver.
B78_SHA = "27062f5e171842bcfa138263a1792856516cea820d15fd1099d152294e6e8e3e"
B78_LEN = 115107

DRY = "--dry" in sys.argv

for a in sys.argv[1:]:
    if a != "--dry":
        SRC = a

with io.open(SRC, "rb") as f:
    raw = f.read()

got = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
print("input  %s" % SRC)
print("       %d bytes  %s" % (len(raw), got))

s = raw.decode("utf-8")

if "g_velapaw_cfg_skip" not in s:
    sys.exit("ABORT: patch #35 is not applied")
if "velapaw_i2s_rx_kick" in s:
    sys.exit("ABORT: patch #36 is already applied")

if len(raw) != B78_LEN or got != B78_SHA:
    sys.exit("ABORT: not the b78 driver\n  want %d  %s\n  got  %d  %s"
             % (B78_LEN, B78_SHA, len(raw), got))


def sub(old, new, what):
    global s
    n = s.count(old)
    if n != 1:
        sys.exit("ABORT: %s -- anchor found %d times, expected 1" % (what, n))
    s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
    print("  ok  %s" % what)


# ------------------------------------------- 1. revert #35 half 1 guards ----

GUARD_RATE = (
    "      /* VelaPaw patch #35: a reconfigure to the value already in effect\n"
    "       * still tears the channel down and resets its FIFO, which orphans\n"
    "       * any in-flight DMA descriptor.  Decline it.  Only skip while the\n"
    "       * channel is started -- if it is stopped nothing is in flight, and\n"
    "       * running the full path guarantees the clock really did get set.\n"
    "       */\n"
    "\n"
    "      if (priv->rate == rate && priv->%s_started)\n"
    "        {\n"
    "          g_velapaw_cfg_skip++;\n"
    "          return rate;\n"
    "        }\n"
    "\n")

GUARD_WIDTH = (
    "      /* VelaPaw patch #35: see i2s_rxsamplerate().  Same reasoning. */\n"
    "\n"
    "      if (priv->data_width == bits && priv->%s_started)\n"
    "        {\n"
    "          g_velapaw_cfg_skip++;\n"
    "          return bits;\n"
    "        }\n"
    "\n")

for what, guard in (("tx samplerate", GUARD_RATE % "tx"),
                    ("rx samplerate", GUARD_RATE % "rx"),
                    ("tx datawidth", GUARD_WIDTH % "tx"),
                    ("rx datawidth", GUARD_WIDTH % "rx")):
    sub(guard, "", "revert #35 guard: %s" % what)

# g_velapaw_cfg_skip now has no writers.  Keep the symbol -- the app externs it
# and prints it, and a permanent 0 is a useful "the guards really are gone".

sub(
    "uint32_t g_velapaw_cfg_skip;  /* same-value reconfigures declined    */\n",
    "uint32_t g_velapaw_cfg_skip;  /* #35 half 1, REVERTED: always 0 now  */\n"
    "uint32_t g_velapaw_rx_kick;   /* velapaw_i2s_rx_kick() calls         */\n",
    "retire cfg_skip, add kick counter")

# ------------------------------------------------- 2. the app-callable kick -

sub(
    "/****************************************************************************\n"
    " * Name: velapaw_sqlen\n",

    "/****************************************************************************\n"
    " * Name: velapaw_i2s_rx_kick\n"
    " *\n"
    " * Description:\n"
    " *   VelaPaw patch #36.  Un-wedge the I2S0 RX path from thread context,\n"
    " *   without going anywhere near the audio upper half.\n"
    " *\n"
    " *   When a capture stalls, mic.c's failure path hangs inside\n"
    " *   mic_session_close() -- the voice worker never returns from\n"
    " *   velapaw_mic_capture() at all, which is why exactly one capture is\n"
    " *   ever attempted per boot.  So recovery cannot be built out of\n"
    " *   AUDIOIOC_STOP / CONFIGURE / START: those are the calls under\n"
    " *   suspicion.  This touches only registers and this driver's own\n"
    " *   queues, so it cannot block.\n"
    " *\n"
    " *   Same hardware sequence as i2s_rx_channel_start(), plus an INT_CLR --\n"
    " *   nothing has cleared the GDMA interrupt status since boot in a stalled\n"
    " *   run, which is why intraw keeps reading the same stale value.\n"
    " *\n"
    " *   Thread context only.  Safe to call when nothing is wrong: the rescue\n"
    " *   loop does not execute and i2s_rxdma_start() returns OK immediately on\n"
    " *   an empty pend queue.\n"
    " *\n"
    " ****************************************************************************/\n"
    "\n"
    "void velapaw_i2s_rx_kick(void)\n"
    "{\n"
    "#ifdef CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0\n"
    "  struct esp32s3_i2s_s *priv = &esp32s3_i2s0_priv;\n"
    "  irqstate_t flags;\n"
    "\n"
    "  if (!priv->config->rx_en)\n"
    "    {\n"
    "      return;\n"
    "    }\n"
    "\n"
    "  flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&priv->slock);\n"
    "\n"
    "  g_velapaw_rx_kick++;\n"
    "\n"
    "  /* Stop RX and its inlink before touching anything else. */\n"
    "\n"
    "  modifyreg32(I2S_RX_CONF_REG(priv->config->port), I2S_RX_START, 0);\n"
    "  SET_GDMA_CH_BITS(DMA_IN_LINK_CH0_REG, priv->dma_channel,\n"
    "                   DMA_INLINK_STOP_CH0_M);\n"
    "\n"
    "  /* Reset the DMA operation, the RX channel and the RX FIFO -- the same\n"
    "   * three resets i2s_rx_channel_start() performs.\n"
    "   */\n"
    "\n"
    "  SET_GDMA_CH_BITS(DMA_IN_CONF0_CH0_REG, priv->dma_channel,\n"
    "                   DMA_IN_RST_CH0_M);\n"
    "  CLR_GDMA_CH_BITS(DMA_IN_CONF0_CH0_REG, priv->dma_channel,\n"
    "                   DMA_IN_RST_CH0_M);\n"
    "\n"
    "  modifyreg32(I2S_RX_CONF_REG(priv->config->port), 0, I2S_RX_RESET);\n"
    "  modifyreg32(I2S_RX_CONF_REG(priv->config->port), I2S_RX_RESET, 0);\n"
    "\n"
    "  modifyreg32(I2S_RX_CONF_REG(priv->config->port), 0, I2S_RX_FIFO_RESET);\n"
    "  modifyreg32(I2S_RX_CONF_REG(priv->config->port), I2S_RX_FIFO_RESET, 0);\n"
    "\n"
    "  modifyreg32(I2S_RX_CONF_REG(priv->config->port), 0, I2S_RX_UPDATE);\n"
    "\n"
    "  /* Drop the stale latched status so the next probe reading means\n"
    "   * something.  Only the ISR ever writes this, and in a stalled run the\n"
    "   * ISR does not run.\n"
    "   */\n"
    "\n"
    "  SET_GDMA_CH_REG(DMA_IN_INT_CLR_CH0_REG, priv->dma_channel, UINT32_MAX);\n"
    "\n"
    "  /* The resets above orphaned anything in flight: owner bit still set, no\n"
    "   * EOF will ever come, and while it sits in rx.act every later\n"
    "   * i2s_rxdma_start() bails at the !sq_empty(&priv->rx.act) test.  Put it\n"
    "   * back at the head of rx.pend, preserving order, and re-arm.\n"
    "   */\n"
    "\n"
    "  while (!sq_empty(&priv->rx.act))\n"
    "    {\n"
    "      sq_addfirst(sq_remlast(&priv->rx.act), &priv->rx.pend);\n"
    "      g_velapaw_rx_resc++;\n"
    "    }\n"
    "\n"
    "  i2s_rxdma_start(priv);\n"
    "\n"
    "  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&priv->slock, flags);\n"
    "#endif /* CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0 */\n"
    "}\n"
    "\n"
    "/****************************************************************************\n"
    " * Name: velapaw_sqlen\n",

    "velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()")

out = s.encode("utf-8")
print("output %d bytes (%+d)" % (len(out), len(out) - len(raw)))

if DRY:
    print("\ndry run clean -- nothing written.")
    sys.exit(0)

tmp = SRC + ".new"
with io.open(tmp, "wb") as f:
    f.write(out)
os.replace(tmp, SRC)

print("\npatch #36 applied.")

THE PROBLEM THIS SOLVES IS NOT THE STALL.

The stall itself is still unexplained and four mechanisms for it are now dead
(TX clock, #31's descriptor desync, #35's redundant reconfigures, and the
`intraw 0xa0` FIFO reading, which turned out to be stale boot-time state).
What b78 established instead is something more immediately actionable:

    caps 1 / lastret -999 / stage 32 (session-close) / lasterr -110

`g_voice_caps` was incremented and `g_voice_lastret` is still its initial
-999, and those two statements are adjacent in the voice worker.  So
velapaw_mic_capture() NEVER RETURNED.  The worker is parked inside
mic_session_close() forever; both "dialog start" entries in the log are the UI
waiting 8 s on a thread that is already gone.

That means exactly ONE capture is attempted per boot, ever.  Nobody has ever
observed what a second attempt would do -- there has never been a second
attempt.  The fault is intermittent, so a retry is very likely worth having,
and it has simply never been reachable.

FIVE CHANGES.

1. Sub-stages 38-44 inside mic_session_close().  Stage 32 covered the entire
   function -- eleven ioctls -- so "hangs at stage 32" localises nothing.  Now
   it will name the ioctl.

2. Stages 34-37 for the recovery path.

3. velapaw_mic_capture() retries in-session on a collect failure, up to
   MIC_KICK_TRIES times, instead of going straight to the teardown that hangs.

   Each retry is: velapaw_i2s_rx_kick() -> flush the mq -> re-arm -> collect
   again.  Deliberately NOT built from AUDIOIOC_STOP / CONFIGURE / START --
   those are the calls under suspicion, and a retry loop made of them would
   hang on its first iteration.  The kick is a patch #36 driver entry point
   that only touches registers and the driver's own queues; it cannot block.

   The kick is declared weak, so this file still links against an unpatched
   driver -- it just degrades to a plain retry.

   The teardown is still there as the last resort.  If all the retries fail we
   are no worse off than b78, and the new sub-stages will at least say where
   it hangs.

4. Two counters, so the probe can distinguish "never needed a kick" from
   "kicked and recovered" from "kicked and still dead".

5. The ordering of quiesce-then-kick matters and is not arbitrary.  A wedged
   container sits in the DRIVER's rx.act: it never completes, never reaches
   rx.done, and never comes back through the message queue -- so mic_quiesce()
   cannot retrieve it, and every subsequent i2s_rxdma_start() bails on the
   `!sq_empty(&priv->rx.act)` test.  Only the kick can empty rx.act.  Hence
   kick BEFORE re-arming, or the re-arm enqueues into a channel that will
   never fire.

Writes <file>.new and os.replace()s it.  --dry checks anchors only.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""VelaPaw b79 -- keep the voice worker alive across a failed capture.

Patches app/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c.  Run on Windows against the D: master tree.
Input must be the b78 ui_lvgl.c (152,566 bytes, the one carrying #35's externs).

WHY.  The worker's failure path was `g_voice_fail = 1; return NULL;` -- one bad
capture and voice is dead for the rest of the boot, with no way back short of a
reboot.  That was a reasonable design when a failed capture meant the mic was
genuinely unusable.  It is the wrong design now that mic.c retries in-session:
after b79's kick loop, a -110 is "this window did not work", not "the microphone
is gone".

It also masked the real behaviour.  The worker never actually reached this code
-- velapaw_mic_capture() hung and never returned -- so `fail 0` in the probe has
been meaningless all along, and the UI's "mic never became ready in 8000ms" was
the only symptom that ever surfaced.  With the hang path now avoided, this code
starts running for the first time, and it should not shoot the thread.

THREE CHANGES.

1. A failed capture is logged, counted and slept off; the worker continues.
   Voice is only disabled after VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL consecutive failures, which
   with mic.c's own MIC_KICK_TRIES means the mic gets 3 x 3 = 9 attempts before
   anything gives up.  A single success anywhere in there resets the count.

2. The 200 ms sleep is not politeness.  Without it a hard failure spins this
   thread against the driver as fast as the timeout allows, and on this board
   that starves the LVGL tick -- the UI would freeze, which is a worse symptom
   than no voice.

3. The probe reports the recovery census: mic-side kicks and their success
   count, and the driver-side kick counter.  cfgskip is retained but now reads
   permanently 0 -- patch #36 reverted #35's guards, so a nonzero value there
   would mean the wrong driver got built.

Writes <file>.new and os.replace()s it.  --dry checks anchors only.
"""

import hashlib
import io
import os
import sys

SRC = r"D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge\app\velapaw\ui\ui_lvgl.c"

B78_SHA = "8a91d64b787c881aa9e16f0f7d58a4b6a1cbaf914b6ef0f8a5a31d5eb8907fb7"
B78_LEN = 152566

DRY = "--dry" in sys.argv

for a in sys.argv[1:]:
    if a != "--dry":
        SRC = a

with io.open(SRC, "rb") as f:
    raw = f.read()

got = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
print("input  %s" % SRC)
print("       %d bytes  %s" % (len(raw), got))

s = raw.decode("utf-8")

if "VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL" in s:
    sys.exit("ABORT: b79 is already applied")

if len(raw) != B78_LEN or got != B78_SHA:
    sys.exit("ABORT: not the b78 ui_lvgl.c\n  want %d  %s\n  got  %d  %s"
             % (B78_LEN, B78_SHA, len(raw), got))


def sub(old, new, what):
    global s
    n = s.count(old)
    if n != 1:
        sys.exit("ABORT: %s -- anchor found %d times, expected 1" % (what, n))
    s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
    print("  ok  %s" % what)


# ------------------------------------------------------- 1. new globals ----

sub(
    "static volatile int   g_voice_lastret = -999;  /* last capture return value   */\n",

    "static volatile int   g_voice_lastret = -999;  /* last capture return value   */\n"
    "\n"
    "/* Build 79.  A failed capture no longer kills the worker, so the failures\n"
    " * have to be counted somewhere instead of being implied by `fail 1`.\n"
    " *\n"
    " * capfail is the running total; consec is the current unbroken run and is\n"
    " * cleared by any success.  Only consec can disable voice -- a total is the\n"
    " * wrong thing to latch on, because a long session that drops one window an\n"
    " * hour is working fine.\n"
    " */\n"
    "\n"
    "static volatile int   g_voice_capfail;         /* captures that failed        */\n"
    "static volatile int   g_voice_consec;          /* ... consecutively, right now */\n"
    "\n"
    "/* Consecutive failures tolerated before voice is declared dead.  mic.c\n"
    " * already retries MIC_KICK_TRIES times inside each call, so this is a\n"
    " * multiplier on that, not the whole budget.\n"
    " */\n"
    "\n"
    "#define VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL 3\n",

    "capfail/consec globals")

# ------------------------------------------------- 2. worker survives ------

sub(
    "      g_voice_lastret = got;\n"
    "      if (got < 0)\n"
    "        {\n"
    "          vlog(\"cap FAILED %d\", got);\n"
    "          printf(\"velapaw/voice: capture failed (%d); voice disabled\\n\", got);\n"
    "          g_voice_fail = 1;\n"
    "          return NULL;\n"
    "        }\n"
    "\n"
    "      g_voice_ready = 1;\n",

    "      g_voice_lastret = got;\n"
    "      if (got < 0)\n"
    "        {\n"
    "          /* Build 79: survive it.  This used to latch g_voice_fail and\n"
    "           * return, which killed voice for the rest of the boot on a\n"
    "           * single bad window.\n"
    "           *\n"
    "           * Worth being clear that this code has never actually run:\n"
    "           * velapaw_mic_capture() hung and never returned, so the probe's\n"
    "           * `fail 0` has been meaningless rather than reassuring.  b79\n"
    "           * removes the hang, so this path executes for the first time --\n"
    "           * and it should not be the thing that shoots the thread.\n"
    "           */\n"
    "\n"
    "          g_voice_capfail++;\n"
    "          g_voice_consec++;\n"
    "\n"
    "          vlog(\"cap FAILED %d (%d in a row)\", got, g_voice_consec);\n"
    "          printf(\"velapaw/voice: capture failed (%d), %d in a row\\n\",\n"
    "                 got, g_voice_consec);\n"
    "\n"
    "          if (g_voice_consec >= VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL)\n"
    "            {\n"
    "              printf(\"velapaw/voice: %d consecutive failures; \"\n"
    "                     \"voice disabled\\n\", g_voice_consec);\n"
    "              g_voice_fail = 1;\n"
    "              return NULL;\n"
    "            }\n"
    "\n"
    "          /* Not politeness.  Without this the thread spins against the\n"
    "           * driver as fast as the timeout allows, and on this board that\n"
    "           * starves the LVGL tick -- a frozen UI is a worse symptom than\n"
    "           * no voice.\n"
    "           */\n"
    "\n"
    "          usleep(200 * 1000);\n"
    "          continue;\n"
    "        }\n"
    "\n"
    "      /* Any success clears the run.  See VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL. */\n"
    "\n"
    "      g_voice_consec = 0;\n"
    "      g_voice_ready = 1;\n",

    "worker survives a failed capture")

# ---------------------------------------------------------- 3. probe -------

sub(
    "/* Patch #35.  cfg_skip counts same-value reconfigures declined, chst counts\n"
    " * real RX channel restarts, resc counts containers pulled back out of rx.act\n"
    " * after a restart orphaned them.  Healthy reads `cfg_skip 3 chst 1 resc 0`.\n"
    " */\n"
    "\n"
    "extern uint32_t g_velapaw_cfg_skip;\n"
    "extern uint32_t g_velapaw_rx_chst;\n"
    "extern uint32_t g_velapaw_rx_resc;\n",

    "/* Patch #35 counters, reinterpreted by patch #36.\n"
    " *\n"
    " * cfgskip must now read 0 -- #36 reverted #35's guards, so anything else\n"
    " * means the wrong driver got linked.  chst counts real RX channel restarts\n"
    " * and resc counts containers pulled back out of rx.act after a reset\n"
    " * orphaned them.\n"
    " */\n"
    "\n"
    "extern uint32_t g_velapaw_cfg_skip;\n"
    "extern uint32_t g_velapaw_rx_chst;\n"
    "extern uint32_t g_velapaw_rx_resc;\n"
    "\n"
    "/* Build 79 recovery census.  kick is the driver-side count of\n"
    " * velapaw_i2s_rx_kick() calls; the mic pair is the app's view of the same\n"
    " * events.  The three readings that matter:\n"
    " *\n"
    " *   mickick 0                nothing ever stalled this boot\n"
    " *   mickick n  ok n          it stalls, and kicking the RX channel clears it\n"
    " *   mickick n  ok 0          it stalls and the kick does nothing, i.e. the\n"
    " *                            fault is below the DMA after all\n"
    " *\n"
    " * The third would be the first hard evidence separating `the DMA got\n"
    " * wedged` from `no samples are arriving`, and it costs one boot to get.\n"
    " */\n"
    "\n"
    "extern uint32_t g_velapaw_rx_kick;\n"
    "extern uint32_t g_mic_kicks;\n"
    "extern uint32_t g_mic_kick_ok;\n",

    "probe externs for the kick counters")

sub(
    "    printf(\"velapaw/voice probe: i2s cfgskip %u chst %u resc %u\\n\",\n"
    "           (unsigned)g_velapaw_cfg_skip, (unsigned)g_velapaw_rx_chst,\n"
    "           (unsigned)g_velapaw_rx_resc);\n",

    "    printf(\"velapaw/voice probe: i2s cfgskip %u chst %u resc %u kick %u\\n\",\n"
    "           (unsigned)g_velapaw_cfg_skip, (unsigned)g_velapaw_rx_chst,\n"
    "           (unsigned)g_velapaw_rx_resc, (unsigned)g_velapaw_rx_kick);\n"
    "    printf(\"velapaw/voice probe: recover mickick %u ok %u  \"\n"
    "           \"capfail %d consec %d\\n\",\n"
    "           (unsigned)g_mic_kicks, (unsigned)g_mic_kick_ok,\n"
    "           g_voice_capfail, g_voice_consec);\n",

    "probe prints the recovery census")

out = s.encode("utf-8")
print("output %d bytes (+%d)" % (len(out), len(out) - len(raw)))

if DRY:
    print("\ndry run clean -- nothing written.")
    sys.exit(0)

tmp = SRC + ".new"
with io.open(tmp, "wb") as f:
    f.write(out)
os.replace(tmp, SRC)

print("\nb79 ui_lvgl.c applied.")
print("       %s" % hashlib.sha256(out).hexdigest())

While that runs — what changed and why:

**The pitch I gave you doesn't survive contact with the code, so I built the corrected version.** "Retry the open until a capture succeeds" assumed a failed capture *returns*. It doesn't. `caps 1` with `lastret -999` means `velapaw_mic_capture()` never came back — the worker is parked inside `mic_session_close()` at stage 32. One capture is attempted per boot, ever; both "dialog start" lines were the UI waiting 8 s on a thread that was already gone. So there's no control flow to retry *from*. The fix has to avoid that path rather than loop around it.

**Four pieces:**

| | change | why |
|---|---|---|
| Driver #36 | revert #35's four config guards | falsified on hardware (`cfgskip 20 chst 1 resc 0`, stall unchanged) — and they suppressed the only thing that ever reset a wedged RX channel |
| Driver #36 | new `velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()` | resets RX + FIFO + GDMA IN, rescues orphaned containers, re-arms. Registers and driver queues only — **cannot block**, unlike STOP/CONFIGURE/START |
| [mic.c](contest2026_043_CircuitForge/app/velapaw/voice/mic.c) | kick → flush → re-arm → re-collect, ×2, before the teardown | the teardown is still there as last resort; it just isn't the first thing tried any more |
| [ui_lvgl.c](contest2026_043_CircuitForge/app/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c) | worker logs + sleeps + continues instead of `return NULL` | that code has never once executed — capture always hung first — so `fail 0` in the probe has been meaningless, not reassuring |

The kick is declared `__attribute__((weak))`, so mic.c still links against an unpatched driver.

**Stage 32 is also split into 38–44.** It covered eleven ioctls, which is why "hangs at stage 32" has told us nothing for three builds. If it still hangs, the next probe names the actual call.

**The measurement this buys, independent of whether it fixes anything:** the probe now prints `mickick N ok M`. `ok = N` means the DMA was wedged and kicking clears it. `ok = 0` means kicking does nothing — which would be the first hard evidence that the fault really is below the DMA, i.e. codec or clock lines, and that the answer is the logic analyzer rather than more driver patches. Either reading is worth one boot.

Assessment, claim by claim.

**The bit naming is wrong, harmlessly.** `I2S_IN_DSCR_EMPTY_INT_RAW` and `INFIFO_UDF_L1` are two different bits — from the VM's own `esp32s3_dma.h`, DSCR_EMPTY is BIT(4) and UDF_L1 is BIT(7). Bit 4 is *clear* in every dump we have. The conclusion it draws (FIFO starved) is still right, just not for the reason of that name.

**The double-enqueue fix is correct** — it matches what I found independently. But "circular reference spinlock within `nxlooper`" is invented. `nxlooper` isn't in this path at all; it's a separate NuttX app. Our chain is mic.c → audio upper half → es8311 → esp32s3_i2s. Right fix, fictional mechanism.

**The phase-slip theory doesn't hold up, and I'd not spend a build on it.** Two reasons:

*RX is the slave here.* An I2S slave receiver frames on WS continuously — every WS edge is a frame boundary, not a one-shot sync pulse to be missed. There's no state where a slave "falls out of step" and stays locked out while WS keeps toggling. The theory needs WS to be a one-time sync, which it isn't.

*It predicts the wrong failure shape.* "Synchronized down to the exact edge transition" predicts deterministic failure. b68 gives `caps 14 / lastret 16000` on a good boot with the identical startup order. Our fault is a coin flip, which this doesn't explain.

**Step A has already been run — this evening.** `modifyreg32(I2S_RX_CONF_REG, 0, I2S_RX_RESET | I2S_RX_FIFO_RESET)` and its clear is exactly what `velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()` does. The probe says `kick 1`, and `intraw` still reads `000000a0` afterwards. That's not a proposal, it's a completed experiment with a negative result.

**Step B isn't implementable as written.** `i2s_rx_channel_start()` never sets `I2S_RX_START` — I read it earlier this session. And TX_START and RX_START are driven from *two different file descriptors* via separate `AUDIOIOC_START` ioctls at different times. Writing TX_START from inside the RX path wouldn't reorder anything; it'd add a second writer firing the TX clock while the TX channel may still be unconfigured.

## What's actually worth taking from it

One real idea, and it's cheaper than the version proposed. `mic_session_open()` issues **`AUDIOIOC_START` on the play fd before the rec fd** — TX before RX, at the application level. That ordering is deliberate and has never been tested against the alternative. Swapping those two calls is a two-line change in mic.c with no driver patch at all.

It may simply fail — RX slaved to a clock that isn't running yet might not arm — but that's a fast, informative answer either way.

So I'd do one more build, containing:

1. **Drop `mic_arm()` from the kick path.** Unambiguously right; the kick already re-armed the driver queues.
2. **Swap the play/rec START order** in `mic_session_open()`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""VelaPaw b80 -- RX starts before TX, and stop retrying inside the call.

Patches app/velapaw/voice/mic.c.  Input must be the b79 mic.c (73,119 bytes).

TWO CHANGES.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. START the record fd BEFORE the playback fd.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

This is the one genuinely untested variable left in the capture path, and it
costs a two-line swap to test.

The existing comment says TX must start first because "without a running TX,
RX never sees a bit clock and the dequeue loop blocks until the timeout with
zero buffers returned".  That observation is real but it is about TX NEVER
running.  It does not say anything about the case this change creates, where
RX is armed a few hundred microseconds BEFORE the clock appears -- there RX
simply waits, and begins framing on the first WS edge it sees.

The theory being tested is that RX must already be listening when the first
clock edge arrives, and that arming it afterwards can leave the deserializer
mis-framed.  I am sceptical of the strong form of that theory: RX here is the
SLAVE (rxconf bit 3 set), and an I2S slave receiver frames on WS continuously
-- every WS edge is a frame boundary, not a one-shot sync pulse that can be
missed.  A slave that is late should re-frame on the next WS, not stay dead.

But the fault is a coin flip, we have never tested this ordering, and every
other hypothesis is now falsified on hardware:

    TX clock / b71 requeue      TX_STOP_EN clear, TX_START set, TX is master
    #31 descriptor desync       miss 0, always
    #35 redundant reconfigures  cfgskip 20, chst 1, stall unchanged
    RX/FIFO/GDMA reset          kick 1, intraw still 000000a0 after it
    lost EOF interrupt          isr 0 with start 2 -- nothing to lose

So: test it.  If RX still never interrupts, the fault is downstream of the
DMA and the next instrument is a scope, not a patch.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Do not retry inside velapaw_mic_capture().  Kick, and return.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

b79's in-call retry loop hung at stage 37 (kick-collect), on both a cold cycle
and a warm reset, at the identical seq 48.  Two things were wrong with it, and
only one of them was the double-enqueue.

  a) DOUBLE ENQUEUE.  velapaw_i2s_rx_kick() re-arms the container it rescued,
     so the driver still owns that buffer.  mic_arm() then enqueued all 18

13	**WORKING on hardware, build 52 (2026-08-05):** live "yes" **0.996**, "no"
14	**0.750**, silence correctly rejected. Every earlier result was weak
15	(b46: yes 0.539, no 0.715) because of the two defects below, both in capture,

17	
18	## 🔴 RX delivers TWO slots and one of them is dead
19	
20	`I2S_RX_MONO` marks the second slot invalid but does **not** remove it from
21	the stream — both slots reach the FIFO and the DMA, with the invalid one
22	zero-filled. Buffers read `[sample, 0, sample, 0, ...]`. This is not 32-bit
23	slot padding: `i2s_set_datawidth()` programs 16-bit slots
24	(`CHAN_BITS = HALF_SAMPLE_BITS = data_width`). It is VelaPaw patch #25:
25	`TOT_CHAN_NUM=1` (two slots) + `CHAN0_EN|CHAN1_EN` + `I2S_RX_MONO`.
26	
27	Consequence: a 16000-`int16` window was **0.5 s of audio with a zero between
28	every sample** — a mirrored spectrum landing inside micro_speech's mel bins.
29	Fix is `MIC_STRIDE 2` — keep one `int16` in two, in `mic_collect()`.
30	
31	### ⚠️ The live slot flips PER CAPTURE, not per build
32	
33	Build 52, one boot: capture 1 slot 0, capture 2 slot 0, capture 3 **slot 1**.
34	Every capture re-arms RX and the first sample lands wherever the frame is.
35	Hardcoding slot 0 makes a capture come back all zeros and look like a dead
36	mic. `mic_data_phase()` measures it, per capture, by counting **exact zeros**
37	— the dead slot is 0 to the bit while the live slot has an ADC noise floor
38	even in a silent room. It returns −1 for an all-zero buffer (RX emits a few
39	while warming up) so the phase is settled off the first buffer with content,
40	not a coin flip.
41	
42	## 🔴 Audio buffers live in PSRAM and the driver does no cache maintenance
43	
44	`apb->samp` addresses are `0x3C5x_xxxx` = the external-memory window
45	(`CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPIRAM=y`, `CONFIG_MM_REGIONS=2`). `esp32s3_i2s.c` has **no**
46	invalidate/writeback/barrier anywhere. So **reusing a buffer inside one
47	window returns a stale cached copy**: first delivery misses cache and reads
48	what DMA wrote, the copy pulls 4 KB into DCache, and ~500 ms later the same
49	buffer hits those warm lines. Signature: an 8-segment profile that repeats
50	with a period equal to the pool depth, and identical samples at the same
51	`apb` pointer.
52	
53	**Fix = never reuse a buffer inside a window.** `GETBUFFERINFO`'s `nbuffers`
54	is a *suggestion*, not a cap — `ALLOCBUFFER` is per-call. `MIC_WANT_BUFS 18`
55	(one delivery = 4092 B = 2046 `int16` = 1023 usable samples after stride, so
56	16000 needs 16 + `MIC_SKIP_BUFS`).
57	
58	### The follow-on trap: a deep pool overruns the quiesce budget
59	
60	Requeueing every accepted buffer left ~17 in flight; one buffer is 128 ms, so
61	draining needs 2.3 s against a 1 s budget sized when the pool was 4. Quiesce
62	timed out, the *next* capture armed with 6 free buffers, and they recycled 3×
63	— reintroducing the cache bug. Two fixes together:
64	- requeue only when `skipped + seq >= nrecbufs - 1` (self-adjusting: a capped
65	  pool still finishes by falling back to recycling)
66	- `MIC_QUIESCE_TRIES 80` (4 s) — a ceiling, not a cost
67

71	(`g_mic`) survive, but **fds do not** — NuttX closes them at task exit, so run

### ✅ SOLVED (b80): the failure path used to be terminal — it isn't now

Two separate terminal behaviours, both fixed:

- `mic_session_close()` **hung** — `lastret -999`, `stage 32`. `g_mic_busy` is
  cleared only after close returns, so every later caller got `-EBUSY` and
  exactly one capture was ever attempted per boot. **Fix (b80): don't close on
  failure.** The `failed:` path now kicks the RX channel, flushes the mq, holds
  the session open, clears `g_mic_busy` and returns the error.
- The voice worker did `g_voice_fail = 1; return NULL;` on any negative
  capture. **Fix (b79):** count failures, sleep 200 ms, `continue`; disable
  voice only after `VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL 3` *consecutive* failures.

b80 confirms both on hardware: `mic stage 33 (done)  lastret -110`, and the
worker logs `cap FAILED -110 (1 in a row)` and lives. **`velapaw_mic_capture()`
returns for the first time.**

⚠️ **But survivability did not buy a retry.** b80 still reads `caps 1
capfail 1 consec 1`. The dialog gives up at **8000 ms** (`mic never became
ready in 8000ms`) while the capture takes **~13 s** to fail — so the capture
returns ~5 s after the dialog window has already closed, and the worker's retry
has no armed dialog to serve. Any future retry work must fix that timing first;
the retry code itself is present and correct.

## 🔴 SIX MECHANISMS FALSIFIED — do not rebuild any of them

All with hardware counters, builds b70–b80. RX arms and its DMA never signals
EOF; nothing reachable from software changes that.

1. **Dead TX ⇒ dead clock / TX requeue (b71).** `TX_STOP_EN` clear, `TX_START`
   set, `SIG_LOOPBACK` set, TX is master. Falsified at the register level.
2. **Descriptor-walk desync (patch #31's missing `else`).** `miss 0` on every
   run, every build. #31 is a defensible latent-bug fix but **not this bug** —
   kept as `patch31-i2s-rx-eof-walk.NOT-APPLIED.py` in the b68 snapshot.
3. **Redundant reconfigures (patch #35 half 1).** b78 measured `cfgskip 20
   chst 1 resc 0` — every redundant reconfigure declined, zero restarts — and
   the stall was unchanged. Reverted by #36.
4. **RX/FIFO/GDMA reset as recovery (patch #36's `velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()`).**
   `kick 1`, `ok 0`. The kick provably runs and clears nothing.
5. **Lost or masked EOF interrupt.** `isr 0` with `start 2` — there is no
   interrupt to lose.
6. **RX-before-TX start ordering (b80).** Started rec fd 200 µs before play fd.
   **Identical** signature: `isr 0 / eof 0 / start 2`, `desc 80000ff0`,
   `intraw 000000a0`. Predicted dead beforehand — RX is the *slave* and an I2S
   slave frames on every WS edge, so there is no one-shot sync to miss.

**CONFIRMED REAL but non-causal:** channel-restart orphaning. b79/b80 read
`chst 11 resc 1` — a restart really does orphan an in-flight container and #35
half 2 really does rescue it. Eliminating it did not fix the stall.

🔴 **The `intraw 000000a0` "stale boot state" reading is WITHDRAWN.** The kick
writes `DMA_IN_INT_CLR = 0xFFFFFFFF` and `kick 1` proves it ran — yet `intraw`
still reads `000000a0` afterwards. Those bits (INFIFO_FULL_WM + INFIFO_UDF_L1)
are **continuously re-asserting**: live evidence of persistent RX FIFO
starvation, not latched history.

Standing signature of the stall, invariant across b76–b80:

    i2s eof 0 match 0 miss 0 empty 0  start 2 busy 1     (or eof 1 / start 3)
    i2s desc 80000ff0 80000010        owner=1, size 4080, length 0
    i2s intraw 000000a0 intena 00000002

Owner bit set with zero bytes written = **the DMA is armed and no samples are
arriving from the codec.** The remaining suspects are below the DMA — ES8311
ADC/clock bring-up or the board's mic path — not the NuttX driver.

Findings are recorded. Here's where b80 leaves us.

## The hang is fixed — that part worked

```
mic stage 33 (done)   lastret -110
log: cap FAILED -110 (1 in a row)
```

For the first time this session `velapaw_mic_capture()` **returns** instead of parking forever. b78 died in `mic_session_close()`, b79 died in `mic_collect`. b80 comes back clean, clears `g_mic_busy`, and the voice worker survives to log the failure. Both survivability changes did exactly what they were built to do.

## The ordering experiment is falsified

Both runs are bit-identical to b78 and b79:

| | b78 | b79 | b80 (RX first) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isr / eof` | 0 or 1 | 0 or 1 | **0 or 1** |
| `desc` | `80000ff0` | `80000ff0` | **`80000ff0`** |
| `intraw` | `000000a0` | `000000a0` | **`000000a0`** |

Starting RX 200 µs before TX changed nothing, which is what I expected — RX is the slave, and an I2S slave frames on every WS edge, so there's no one-shot sync to miss. Run 1 is `isr 0` with `start 2`: the DMA is armed, the descriptor still owns its buffer with **zero bytes written**, and no interrupt ever comes. That's the stop criterion I named last turn, and it's met.

## One thing I hadn't seen before

`caps 1 / capfail 1 consec 1` — the worker's 3-try retry never fired. The reason is in the log timestamps:

```
47220  === dialog start ===
55250  mic never became ready in 8000ms     <- dialog gives up
60570  cap FAILED -110                       <- capture returns, 5s too late
```

The capture takes **~13 s** to fail against the dialog's **8 s** patience. So the retry path is live and correct but structurally unreachable — by the time it could run, there's no armed dialog to serve. Fixing that is a timing change, not a DMA change, and it would only buy three failures instead of one.

## Recommendation: freeze voice, reflash b68

Six mechanisms are now dead with hardware evidence — TX clock, descriptor desync, redundant reconfigures, RX/FIFO/GDMA reset, lost EOF, start ordering. The surviving signature (owner bit set, length 0, `INFIFO_UDF` re-asserting) says the DMA is armed and **no samples are arriving from the codec**. That's below the driver, and I have no software lever left that I believe in.

**Flash `nuttx-b68rebuild.bin`, not b80.** b80 is better engineering but it's the riskier demo image: b68 has *proven* successful captures on a good boot (`caps 14`, `lastret 16000`), and b80 has never captured successfully even once — the RX-first swap is untested on a good boot and could have broken the working path. For a demo you want the image with observed wins.

Two things worth saying before I act:

1. If you want the polish, there's a **b81** = b68's proven start order + b80's graceful-failure path, no ordering change. On a good boot voice works; on a bad boot it fails cleanly instead of parking a thread. That's one more build and it's strictly the best demo image. But the hung thread in b68 is invisible to a viewer — the UI stays fine — so this is optional, not needed.
2. Reflashing changes the board state, so I'll wait for your word rather than assume.

Say **"b68"** and I'll flash it and pivot to assembly, the two JLC reviewer replies (Order 1 G26080101901 / 周泽平; Order 2 G26080101873 / 李璟卓), and docs. Say **"b81"** and I'll build the merged image first.

look at this and recommend: The structural recovery logic is now fully operational. Safely unwinding the double-enqueue bug has decoupled the software layer from the hardware freeze, allowing velapaw_mic_capture() to successfully clear its busy flags, preserve the voice worker context, and return a clean execution trace.
Your assertion about the clock framing is also spot-on: because the slaved RX interface continuously resets its phase tracking on every Word Select (WS) edge, shifting the start order by 200 µs could not have solved a framing offset.
The fact that intraw remains locked at 000000a0 while the descriptor retains ownership (owner=1) with zero bytes written confirms our definitive stop criterion: the digital audio data streams are physically absent from the hardware pin boundary.
## 1. The Timing Disconnect Explains the Single Failure
The reason your 3-try loop never gets a chance to rescue the stream is that the upper-half context is being destroyed out from under it:

* The Upper-Half Trap: nxlooper or the underlying POSIX message queue block is configured to block or timeout over a window that totals roughly 13 seconds.
* The Application Drop: The high-level voice dialog engine uses an independent, strict 8-second execution timer.
* The Result: At 8000ms, the dialog engine assumes the system has completely locked up, aborts the session, and breaks the audio pipeline bindings. When the lower-half driver finally unblocks at 13,000ms, it attempts to return data to a dead, dismantled upper-half state machine.

To make your survivability loop reachable, you must squeeze the lower-half timeout so it fires before the application loses patience.
## 2. Shifting the Focus Downstream: The Codec Side
Since the Espressif GDMA engine is completely clean and the I2S receiver is actively pulling from the FIFO, the persistent zero-byte capture confirms that the ES8311 codec chip itself is not outputting data on its Serial Data Out (SDOUT) pin.
Because this behavior is deeply tied to a warm reset, the codec's internal state machine is likely retaining a shutdown or muted configuration flag.
## The LDO Power-Down Theory
During a taping reset, the ESP32 drops its GPIO outputs. If the codec's analog or digital supply domains are gated by an external regulator or an active-low shutdown pin tied to a floating or pulled-down ESP32 GPIO, the ES8311 drops into a partial sleep state. When the CPU wakes up, it re-initializes the control registers over I2C, but the internal analog-to-digital converter (ADC) clock tree remains power-gated.
## The System Control Register Latch
The ES8311 has specific power-management registers (Registers 0x01 to 0x0D) that handle the operational bias currents for the microphone amplifier and ADC components. If a warm reset cuts off the clock stream abruptly mid-flight, the ES8311's internal control registers can latch into an un-synchronized power-saving protection mode.
## 3. Implementing the Next Iteration
To resolve the timing mismatch and force a clean failure cascade (verifying your 3-try loop), we need a dual-pronged fix in your next build:
## Change A: Pull the Driver Timeout Inside the 8-Second Window
In your lower-half I2S driver configuration or the nxlooper worker loop, locate the blocking read/timeout threshold. Reduce the hardware collection block timeout down to 2000ms or 3000ms.

* This ensures that when the FIFO is starved, the driver fails and triggers its first recovery kick well within the 8-second application ceiling, keeping the dialog engine alive.

## Change B: Inject a Explicit Power-Down/Power-Up Cycle over I2C
Since we know the problem lies inside the codec, we must force its internal power rails to clean-start during initialization. At the beginning of es8311_configure (right around your reset calls), explicitly cycle the chip's power control structures:

/* Force power down of the analog and digital core blocks over I2C */
es8311_write_reg(priv, 0x01, 0xFF); // Turn off all internal master clocks
es8311_write_reg(priv, 0x02, 0x00); // Power down digital circuits
up_mdelay(10);                      // Let internal capacitance discharge
/* Enforce a clean power up sequence */
es8311_write_reg(priv, 0x01, 0x00); // Re-enable master clocks
es8311_write_reg(priv, 0x02, 0x80); // Power up internal digital core

Once you scale back the lower-half collection timeout to bring it safely under the 8-second window:

* Does the voice worker now successfully cycle through all 3 retry attempts before the dialog engine times out?
* If you monitor the es8311 configuration pass, are there any custom register overrides being written to the chip's ADC power control blocks that might be skipping initialization on a warm reboot?

Assessed against what we've actually measured. Two of its claims are right, one is fatally wrong, and the code block would make things worse — but there's one genuinely good idea buried in it that I want to extract.

## Verdict

| Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Structural recovery works; capture returns clean | ✅ Correct — matches `stage 33 (done) / lastret -110` |
| 200 µs reorder couldn't fix framing (slave re-syncs on WS) | ✅ Correct |
| Data is physically absent at the pin boundary | ✅ Agreed — that's my read of `owner=1, length 0` too |
| The 13 s / 8 s mismatch starves the retry loop | ✅ Correct **as an observation** (it's mine from last turn) — ❌ wrong on mechanism |
| "nxlooper or the POSIX mq blocks for ~13 s" | ❌ **nxlooper is not in this path.** Second time this source has invented it |
| Dialog timeout "breaks the audio pipeline bindings" | ❌ It doesn't. The dialog closes a UI window; the mic session belongs to the worker thread and is untouched |
| "Deeply tied to a warm reset" → LDO power-down theory | ❌ **Fatal.** This is the load-bearing premise and it's false |
| System Control Register Latch (same premise) | ❌ Dies with it |
| The REG01/REG02 code block | ❌ Wrong registers, and the comments are inverted |

## The fatal one

Everything downstream of §2 rests on *"this behavior is deeply tied to a warm reset."* It isn't. We confirmed on 2026-08-07 that **cold power cycles fail too** — and b80's run 2 *was* a cold cycle: `isr 1 / eof 1 / start 3`, same stall. A cold cycle removes power from the codec entirely. If a full power removal doesn't clear it, no amount of "the LDO stayed gated across a warm reset" can be the story. Both codec-latch theories are dead on arrival.

## The code block would break the working DAC

On the ES8311, **REG01 and REG02 are the clock manager, not power control.** REG01's bits are the MCLK/BCLK/ADC-clock *enables*, so the comments are backwards in both directions: `0xFF` turns clocks **on** (labelled "turn off"), and `0x00` turns them **off** (labelled "re-enable master clocks"). Dropping that into `es8311_configure()` would leave the codec with its clock tree gated — a guaranteed dead ADC, and probably a dead DAC too, killing the playback path that currently works. Actual ES8311 power control lives in **REG0D / REG0E / REG12 / REG13**. The accessor is also `es8311_writereg()` in this tree, not `es8311_write_reg()` — the snippet wasn't checked against the source.

**Do not apply Change B.** Change A (shrink the collect timeout) is harmless but buys only three failures in 8 s instead of one in 13 — the in-session re-arm is already proven dead at `ok 0`.

## The one idea worth keeping

Stripped of the wrong mechanism, its closing question is the right one: **we have never once read the ES8311's state back.** Every codec claim in this whole investigation — including mine — is inferred from I2S counters. We've been debugging the listener, never the talker.

And it's unusually cheap to fix, because **the app already talks I2C directly** — that's how the PCF85063 RTC works. So I can extend the `velapaw voice` probe to read ES8311 (0x18) registers **0x0D, 0x0E, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14, 0x17, 0x44** straight off the bus. That's an app-only change: no driver patch, no audio-path change, nothing that can regress the working image.

It's genuinely decisive either way:

- **ADC power/bias bits wrong on a stalled boot** → we've found it after nine builds, and it's a register write to fix.
- **Bits correct** → the codec is configured and emitting, the fault is analog or the mic itself, and voice is a hardware problem we cannot close before the deadline. That's a real answer, not another dead end.

Caveat: the audio driver owns that bus. NuttX serializes per-bus with a semaphore so a concurrent read is safe, same as the RTC does — but I'd read only, never write.

## Recommendation

**Flash b68 now, and treat the codec read-back as the single optional last experiment.**

Nothing in this suggestion changes the freeze decision — its two fixable proposals are one no-op and one regression. But the read-back is one app-only build with no risk to the demo image, and it converts "unknown" into "found it" or "it's hardware." That's worth having in the write-up either way.

If the deadline is tight, skip it. Assembly, the two JLC replies (Order 1 G26080101901 / 周泽平; Order 2 G26080101873 / 李璟卓), and docs are worth more than a ninth voice build.

Say **"b68"** to flash and pivot, or **"b68 + probe"** to flash b68 and build the read-back probe alongside it.

I read the actual constants, and this is a better question than I gave it credit for. The numbers are worse than I said, and there's a real bug here that has nothing to do with the DMA.

## The two timeouts are the same number

```
ui_lvgl.c:613    #define VOICE_CAPTURE_MS   8000   // given to velapaw_mic_capture()
ui_lvgl.c:2735   #define VSCHED_MIC_WAIT_MS 8000   // dialog's patience for g_voice_ready
```

The dialog gives the capture *exactly* as long as the capture gives itself — but the capture's clock starts later, because it pays session-open first. The dialog can therefore **never** win. It's not a tuning mismatch, it's structurally guaranteed.

The measured decomposition confirms it: dialog starts 47220, gives up at 55250 (= +8030 ✓), capture returns 60570. So session open = 60570 − 47220 − 8000 = **5350 ms**, then an 8000 ms collect timeout on top.

## The part that matters: this bites the *working* path too

Look at [ui_lvgl.c:2780-2806](D:/openVela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge/app/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c#L2780-L2806) — the dialog deliberately refuses to prompt until the first capture proves the mic is open (`vsched_prompt(); /* now it is a fair question to ask */`). Sound design. But price it on a **good** boot:

```
5350 ms   session open  (es8311 configure, 11 channel restarts, 19 buffers)
+2000 ms  first capture returns as soon as it has 32000 samples
=7350 ms  vs. an 8000 ms deadline
```

**650 ms of margin.** Any jitter in session open — a codec retry, scheduler noise, one extra reconfigure — and the dialog prints "mic never became ready" *while the microphone is working perfectly*.

That reframes something. We have been attributing every failed dialog to the DMA stall. Some fraction of them were probably this instead, and it would look identical from the outside.

## The fix, in the right order

**1. Pre-open the session in the voice worker's init, not lazily on first capture.** [mic.c:1846](D:/openVela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge/app/velapaw/voice/mic.c#L1846) opens on demand; [mic.c:1029](D:/openVela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge/app/velapaw/voice/mic.c#L1029) already says *"Called once per boot."* Move it to boot. The 5350 ms leaves the dialog's critical path entirely, and good-boot margin goes from 650 ms to ~6 s — **9× more headroom.**

⚠️ It must be opened **by the worker thread itself**, not from `main()` — `g_mic.owner = getpid()`, and an owner mismatch triggers the drop-and-reopen path, which is the `-110` reopen bug.

**2. Then, and only then, split the timeouts.** With setup off the path, `VOICE_CAPTURE_MS 3500` fits two full attempts (3.5 + 0.2 + 3.5 = 7.2 s) inside the 8 s window. That's the retry loop the external suggestion was chasing — reached correctly, by removing setup rather than by squeezing the driver.

Note this is the *opposite* of Change A in that suggestion. Shrinking the collect timeout alone would fire retries into a window still half-consumed by session open. The setup cost has to go first or the tuning is meaningless.

The stale-artifact clear matters more than usual this time — **`mic.h` changed**, and header edits don't reliably trigger rebuilds in this tree.

No driver patch in b81, so the VM keeps the b79/b80 `esp32s3_i2s.c`. Patch #36's kick stays linked but inert, which is what we want: it costs nothing and keeps the `kick`/`chst`/`resc` counters reporting.

## What went in

| # | Change | File |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reverted b80's RX-first start order → TX-first | `voice/mic.c` |
| 2 | `velapaw_mic_preopen()` + `g_mic_fresh` double-enqueue guard | `voice/mic.c`, `mic.h` |
| 3 | Worker pre-opens the session at init | `ui/ui_lvgl.c` |
| 4 | `VOICE_CAPTURE_MS` 8000 → 3500 | `ui/ui_lvgl.c` |

Two things worth flagging from writing it:

**I renamed the function.** `velapaw_mic_open` collides as a substring with the existing `struct velapaw_mic_open_s` and `velapaw_mic_open_log` — no C-level conflict, but a new function sitting next to the open-*logging* struct with a near-identical name is a trap for the next reader. It's `velapaw_mic_preopen()`.

**The double-enqueue guard is the load-bearing part.** `mic_session_open()` leaves 19 buffers armed and in flight — that's why the inline-open path goes straight to collect while the already-open path does flush+arm. A pre-opened session would have hit the second branch and enqueued on top of buffers the driver still held. `g_mic_fresh` makes the first capture after a pre-open take the open path's behaviour, so the proven sequence is unchanged — just earlier in time.

## Item 5 is not in this build

The ES8311 read-back needs the I2C bus handle, and the only reference in the app points at the board file ([ui_lvgl.c:254](D:/openVela/contest2026_043_CircuitForge/app/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c#L254): *"I2C in the board file"*). Adding it means a board-file change, which breaks the app-only, can't-regress-the-driver property that makes b81 safe to try. I've left it out rather than quietly widening the blast radius — it's a b82 on its own if you want it.

## What to read on the probe

- `preopen 0` — the session was open before any dialog could ask. If it's non-zero, the pre-open failed and the first capture opened inline, so the margin is back to what it was and the rest of the test is void.
- `capms 3500 dialogms 8000` — confirms the two numbers are no longer equal.
- **`caps` reaching 2 or 3** — the retry loop executing for the first time.
- `chst` / `resc` / `kick` as before.

Expect the stall itself to be unchanged — b78 already falsified the settling theory at `chst 1`. What b81 is really testing is whether good boots get more reliable, and whether the retry is finally reachable.

## 🔴 THE TWO TIMEOUTS WERE THE SAME NUMBER (b81 fixes this)

Independent of the DMA stall, and it bit the path that **works**:

    ui_lvgl.c:613    VOICE_CAPTURE_MS   8000   given to velapaw_mic_capture()
    ui_lvgl.c:2735   VSCHED_MIC_WAIT_MS 8000   dialog's patience for ready

The dialog gave the capture exactly as long as the capture gave itself — while
the capture's clock started *later*, after `mic_session_open()`. The dialog can
therefore **never** outlast a failing capture. Structural, not a tuning miss.

**Session open measures 5350 ms** on this board (b80: dialog start 47220, gave
up 55250 = +8030, capture returned 60570 = +13350; 13350 − 8000 = 5350).

So a **good** boot had `5350 + 2000 = 7350` against an 8000 ms deadline —
**650 ms of margin** — and `vsched_tick()` only prompts the user *after* the
first capture proves the mic open. Any jitter printed "mic never became ready"
**while the microphone was working perfectly.** Some fraction of failures
blamed on the DMA stall were probably this; from outside they look identical.

b81 fixes it in the only order that works:
1. **`velapaw_mic_preopen()`** — worker opens the session at init, moving the
   5350 ms to boot. Margin 650 ms → ~6 s. Must be called **by the capturing
   thread** (session is owned by pid; mismatch = the `-110` reopen path).
   Non-fatal: on failure the first capture opens inline exactly as before.
2. **`VOICE_CAPTURE_MS` 8000 → 3500** — two attempts now fit in the dialog's
   window (3500 + 200 + 3500 = 7200), finally making b79's retry reachable.
   Doing (2) without (1) is pointless — retries fire into a half-eaten window.

🔴 **The `g_mic_fresh` double-enqueue guard is load-bearing.**
`mic_session_open()` returns with 19 buffers **already armed and in flight** —
which is why the inline-open path goes straight to collect while the
already-open path does flush + arm. A pre-opened session would take the second
branch and enqueue on top of buffers the driver still holds. `g_mic_fresh`
marks "opened, never captured from" so the first capture skips the re-arm.

⚠️ Name trap: `velapaw_mic_open` is a **substring of the existing**
`struct velapaw_mic_open_s` and `velapaw_mic_open_log`, so a `grep`-style
"already applied?" guard false-positives on it. The function is
`velapaw_mic_preopen()`.

⚠️ `mic_status()` tag literals (`"rec enq"`, `"rec start"`, `"rec fresh"`…) are
**optimized out of the image** — they read 0 under `grep -a` in b80 *and* b81.
Do not use them as build-verification markers; use a `printf` string instead.

A complete spoken meal-scheduling dialog, committed. And the I2S state is the cleanest this board has ever produced.

## The timing fix is proven

This is the number that settles it:

```
59760  cap 16000 in 1230ms
61210  cap 16000 in 1230ms
62440  cap 16000 in 1230ms
...    ten captures, 58.5s → 71.3s
```

**Every capture returns in 1230 ms.** In b80, *one* capture consumed the entire 8000 ms window and returned 5 s after the dialog had given up. Here the dialog ran ten captures inside that same window and never once printed "mic never became ready." That's the 5350 ms of session open moving to boot, doing exactly what it was designed to do.

`preopen 0` confirms the pre-open executed. And 1230 ms against the new 3500 ms timeout is **2.8× margin**, so shrinking it was empirically safe — that was the change I was least sure of.

## The I2S counters have never looked like this

| | stalled boots (b76–b80) | **b81 now** |
|---|---|---|
| `eof / match` | 0–1 | **364 / 364** |
| `intraw` | `000000a0` | **`00000000`** |
| `desc` | `80000ff0` (owner=1, len 0) | **`00000000`** |
| `act / pend` | 1 / 1 | **0 / 0** |
| `resc` (at `chst 11`) | 1 | **0** |
| `capfail` | 1 | **0** |

Zero rescues needed despite eleven channel restarts, and `lasterr 0` — not a single error the whole boot.

## What I am *not* claiming

**The stall is not proven fixed.** It didn't happen this boot, and it was always intermittent — my own rule from earlier in this investigation is that a single passing boot proves nothing and only counters across boots do. b81 contains no change that should plausibly affect the DMA, and b78 already falsified the settling theory. The honest reading is: **the timing bug is fixed and confirmed; the stall is untested because it didn't fire.**

Testing that costs nothing now — no rebuild, just **4–5 cold power cycles, dialog each time**. If `capfail 0` holds across all of them, that's a real signal. If one stalls, we'll now see `caps` climb to 2–3 with the retry actually firing, which is data we've never had.

## Two things worth your call

**Did you say "two"/"eight", or "one"/"nine"?** The log heard `one 0.469` and `nine 0.535` → 09:00. If you said one/nine, recognition is fine. If you said two/eight, it misheard both digits and that's a separate accuracy problem worth knowing before a demo.

**Step 3 needed four utterances** — `no 0.066` → `yes 0.348` → `yes 0.547` → `yes 0.797 OK`. The third missed the 0.55 gate by **0.003**. A judge saying "yes" four times is a bad demo moment. Also worth noting: the vote rule rescued step 2 (`0.527 LOW but 2 votes -> accept`) but stayed at `v0` through three step-3 readings including two "yes" — that asymmetry looks inconsistent and may be a real gap in the vote logic. I'd leave both alone for now rather than retune a working build on one sample, but flag it as the next thing to look at if the demo feels sticky.

# b81 "preopen" — the shipping voice build

**Snapshot 2026-08-07.** This is the image to demo. Verified on hardware with a
complete spoken dialog: `COMMIT meal 1 = 09:00`.

Everything here is plain file copies. There is no git involved, deliberately.

---

## Status: what this build does and does not do

**Voice scheduling works, on roughly 3 cold boots in 5.**

The remaining 2-in-5 is the long-standing I2S RX stall — the first capture of a
boot arms the DMA and no samples ever arrive from the codec. b81 does not fix
that and was never expected to; six software mechanisms for it are falsified
with hardware counters (see the `velapaw-mic-capture` memory). It is
intermittent and per-boot: a boot is either good for its whole life or bad from
the first capture.

**What b81 DID fix — and this is confirmed, not inferred —** is a separate
timing bug that was costing good boots:

    VOICE_CAPTURE_MS   8000   given to velapaw_mic_capture()
    VSCHED_MIC_WAIT_MS 8000   the dialog's patience

Identical numbers, while the capture's clock started ~5350 ms later because it
paid `mic_session_open()` first. The dialog could never outlast a failing
capture, and on a *good* boot it had only 650 ms of margin — so ordinary jitter
printed "mic never became ready" while the microphone was working perfectly.

b81 moves session open to boot (`velapaw_mic_preopen()`, called by the voice
worker) and cuts `VOICE_CAPTURE_MS` to 3500. Measured result: every capture now
returns in **1230 ms**, and one dialog made **ten** captures inside the same
8000 ms window that previously fit exactly one.

### Demo protocol

Because a bad boot is bad from its first capture, check before you present:

1. Cold power cycle (RTS reset does not boot the app over USB-JTAG).
2. Open My Pets → Edit, say one word, confirm it is heard.
3. If it times out, power cycle and repeat. Two tries ≈ 84%, three ≈ 94%.

🔴 Do **not** run `velapaw kws mic` before the dialog in the same boot — it
poisons the session via the `-110` reopen bug and invalidates the test.

### Reading the probe (`velapaw voice`)

Healthy boot:

    caps 19  lastret 16000   preopen 0  capms 3500  dialogms 8000
    mic stage 33 (done)  lasterr 0
